label: Coffee she isn't drinking
alt: Etta Ray sits alone at the kitchen table of her Bed-Stuy flat holding a cup of coffee she is not drinking, the front door open behind her onto the stairwell.
note: The film's first cut away from the laundromat: no music, no dialogue, a woman sitting still while her building moves carefully around her.

label: The signature
alt: Two uniformed officers wait in the open doorway of the Ray flat with a clipboard form while, out of focus on the landing behind them, a covered stretcher is carried down the stairs; Etta signs with a pen that has run out of ink.
note: Covers the officers' lines and Etta's. The pen running dry is the beat: she presses hard enough to leave her name in the paper.

label: Thumb over PLAY
alt: Bug Ray stands in the bedroom doorway hugging the shoebox cassette recorder, his thumb hovering over the PLAY button without pressing it.
note: Holds through the FREEZE and the SWEET JESUS title card. He never presses play here; the film cuts away instead.

label: He fixed my window
alt: A Halloween mask hanging from the fire escape; Jack Monroe waits on the stoop with a paper twist of sunflower seeds in his breast pocket and looks up as Etta Ray comes out of the door behind him.
note: Jack has just spat shells into the gutter. Etta's first line to him is a refusal of condolence, so the frame keeps both of them and the distance between them.

label: A shell on the step
alt: The coroner's van pulls away from the kerb while Bug watches from the doorway hugging the recorder and Jack, on the stoop, scrapes a sunflower seed shell off his shoe on the stone step.
note: Ends the scene: Jack has no answer to Etta's question, Etta goes inside, and he is left with a shell stuck to his shoe.

label: Behind the line she gave him
alt: In the green-tiled morgue corridor, Etta stands at the high wooden counter while a clerk in a white jacket slides a personal-effects list towards her; Jack stands two paces behind her, hands empty, staying behind the line she gave him.
note: Jack's position in this frame is the scene: he does not step up to the counter for the rest of it.

label: A pencilled thirteen
alt: Tight insert on the morgue counter: the personal-effects list, one empty glassine bag, a set of keys and the pink laundry receipt with a navy-yard address and a pencilled circled thirteen, as Etta signs the release with a dry pen.
note: The insert that starts the investigation. Jack's eye is on the receipt, not on Etta.

label: Copied onto the wrapper
alt: Close insert of Jack's hands copying the navy-yard address in pencil onto the back of an opened brown paper sunflower-seed twist, the laundry receipt and a few spilled shells beside it on the counter.
note: He asks before he takes the receipt, and copies the address rather than keeping the original.

label: A reminder on the desk
alt: Jack's shabby one-room office in late morning: he stands at the sticking sash window with his back three-quarters to camera, while in the foreground on the battered desk lie an empty glassine bag and a torn note printed in blue ballpoint capitals.
note: The desk is dressed before Pike is revealed: Jack has not turned round to look at it yet.

label: That's not evidence
alt: Lieutenant Frank Pike stands at his ease by the green filing cabinet, coat open over a rumpled suit, while Jack stands between him and the desk without touching the glassine bag and the note lying on it.
note: Covers the whole confrontation. Jack never touches the bag; Pike watches the effort it costs him.
